title: Black-box conversion to dominant-strategy truthfulness without expected-welfare loss
area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
formal: Can a polynomial-query black-box transformation turn any allocation algorithm under independent known single-parameter value distributions into a dominant-strategy truthful-in-expectation mechanism preserving its expected welfare?

import_provenance.original_title: Black-box conversion to dominant-strategy truthfulness without expected-welfare loss
import_provenance.original_statement: Can a polynomial-query black-box transformation turn any allocation algorithm for independent, known single-parameter value distributions into a truthful-in-expectation dominant-strategy mechanism preserving its expected welfare? The transformation learns feasibility only from the allocation algorithm’s outputs; the benchmark is average welfare under the prior, not a worst-case approximation guarantee.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Bayesian incentive-compatible reductions are known, and stronger MIDR reductions or preservation of worst-case approximation are impossible; neither answers this expected-welfare DSIC question.
